# Decades-long victory, bold Apple survey findings, legal workshop success & our 50th podcast episode - FSFE

[News](https://fsfe.org/news/news.en.html)

## Digital Sovereignty needs Free Software

In the last weeks, we got the green light to intervene

against Apple before the European Court of Justice for the second time

(!) while the European Commission has included the “Public Money? Public

Code!” principle in its Technological Sovereignty

Package. And stay tuned! A new European consortium will be launching soon, and we are part of it!

This month is starting with good news: the European Commission

included the Free Software Foundation Europe’s “Public Money? Public

Code!” principle in the newly released Technological Sovereignty

Package, which also contains the new "Open Source Strategy". If

implemented, it could mark a paradigm shift towards making publicly

financed software available as Free Software. But it is too early to

lean back: [Its success

will depend on binding rules, long-term funding, and meaningful civil

society involvement](https://fsfe.org/news/2026/news-20260603-01.en.html).

However, not all public administrations think the same: England’s

National Health Service (NHS England) has made most of its public source

code repositories private by default, based on concerns that public code

repositories could be scanned by AI systems to identify vulnerabilities.

At the FSFE we were clear about it: [NHS England

should not hide public code behind closed doors](https://fsfe.org/news/2026/news-20260504-01.en.html). De-publishing does

not make code unseen, nor does it remove existing copies, and it is not

an effective security measure. Instead, it removes a fundamental pillar

for security: the ability of independent experts, researchers, and other

public bodies to inspect, reuse, and improve the code, and to report on

security issues.

We called on the Free Software community to push that decision back

by signing [an open letter to NHS

England,](https://keepthingsopen.com/)calling on them to keep their code open. The community’s

response was strong, with more than 500 additional signatures in the

hours after our call. Shortly afterwards, the UK Government Digital

Service issued new guidance making clear that public bodies should keep

code public by default.

Digital sovereignty through Free Software was also the topic of our

latest Software Freedom Podcast episode, in which Bonnie and Johannes talk with

Petteri from X-Road about the current challenges

for Free Software projects in public administrations. [Listen to it!](https://fsfe.org/news/podcast/2026/episode-51.en.html)

You may already know that despite

the need for digital sovereignty in Europe, [funding

for European projects such as the Next Generation Internet Zero (NGI0)

programme was cut](https://fsfe.org/news/2024/news-20240719-01.en.html). We're glad to share some good news on this

front: we recently announced a new European consortium for a resilient,

home-grown technology European ecosystem: the Restack project.

Operating under Horizon Europe, [the FSFE

is a partner of this cascade funding programme, designed to retain the

strength of the NGI Zero approach](https://fsfe.org/news/2026/news-20260528-01.en.html). Our role will be to provide legal

and licensing support for potentially over 200 Free Software projects

and assist their growth into part of a wider European digital

commons.

### Defending interoperability in Europe

> “With industry interests well represented by several interveners on
> the other side, the FSFE is there to ensure that civil society is
> equally heard — and that the court can decide with the full picture
> before it" Dr. Martin Husovec, the lawyer representing FSFE in
> the case T-359/25 - Apple against the European Commission

In a landmark development for Software Freedom in Europe,

the Free Software Foundation Europe has been granted permission

to intervene at the Court of Justice of the European Union in the case

T-359/25 - Apple against the European Commission. This intervention aims

to defend interoperability and Software Freedom in Europe and it is the

second time the FSFE is intervening in a litigation at the CJEU in

regards to the DMA and Apple. [The

previous case (T-1080/23](https://fsfe.org/activities/apple-litigation/apple-litigation.en.html)) concerns Apple’s broader challenge to its

DMA obligations and its designation as gatekeeper, while this case

(T-359/25) focuses specifically on interoperability under Article 6(7)

DMA and the legality of the European Commission’s decision specifying

how Apple must implement those obligations in practice.

Following our work on the Digital Markets Act, we participated in the

[SCiDA

Conference](https://scidaproject.com/2025/10/23/call-for-abstracts-scida-conference-on-shaping-competition-in-the-digital-age-towards-best-practices/) in Düsseldorf, a leading academic event focused on

competition in digital markets. There, the FSFE was invited to present

its work on interoperability in Android during a plenary session,

highlighting the relevance of our work within ongoing policy and

academic discussions.

The conference brought together senior representatives from

competition authorities across Europe as well as members of the European

Commission's DMA enforcement team. The conference provided an excellent

opportunity to strengthen connections with key stakeholders and to

further raise awareness of the FSFE's policy work on digital markets and

users' freedom to control their devices.

Up for learning more about the DMA? We were

invited for [episode 5 of the

"DMA Vox Populi" podcast about the DMA review](https://media.fsfe.org/w/j1CDP2zKnH1Px5fKKnvsvM%C3%A7). There, Dario

discusses what the European Commission got right, where it fell short,

and what must come next for software freedom and interoperability in

Europe.

### Youth Hacking 4 Freedom 2026

The 2026 edition of [Youth

Hacking 4 Freedom](https://yh4f.org) is reaching its peak. The programming period wraps up at

the end of this month, and while participants can finally catch their

breath, the jury will be getting to work evaluating their projects. In

October, we will meet the 6 winners of this edition at the Award

Ceremony weekend in Brussels.

For the fifth edition of YH4F we had over 80 participants from 21

countries! 😮 We can't wait to see what they have developed. And we are already planning

for the next edition, so stay tuned!

### From the stages: Ada, Digital Sovereignty, PIWO and more!

May has been a busy month! Our Polish local group took part in

P.I.W.O. (the Poznań Free Software Event), where volunteers ran a booth

promoting Free Software. And while the name might make us think of free

"piwo" (that's beer in Polish), what participants got was free pizza.

In Berlin our group

organized a Linux presentation day in which

people could try Linux laptops and get all their questions answered

about them.

Moreover, besides attending SCIDA, we participated in a panel about

the DMA in Brussels. During the CPDP conference, we sat in the [panel](https://www.cpdpconferences.org/panels/it-takes-two-to-tango-public-and-private-enforcement-of-the-digital-markets-act)

[entitled

"It takes two to tango: Public and private enforcement of the Digital

Markets Act](https://www.cpdpconferences.org/panels/it-takes-two-to-tango-public-and-private-enforcement-of-the-digital-markets-act)" at the CPDP conference, where we presented our work on

the DMA enforcement, including our [litigation

against Apple at the European Union Court of Justice](https://fsfe.org/activities/apple-litigation/apple-litigation.en.html).

Digital sovereignty was

also the topic in a lecture series in

Regensburg, where, after watching the animated movie “Ada &

Zangemann”, we took part in a discussion about this topic.

**The FSFE is turning 25! And we want to celebrate it with

you!** Join us on 18 and 19 July in Cracow for a weekend

full of Free Software with talks, networking, and of course, a cake! Wanna

know more? Write us: contact@fsfe.org

Ada was also present at

several events: we had a movie screening and

a kids' workshop at the Tübingen Digital Freedom Days, where we also ran

a booth. In Utrecht, at the NLUUG conference, our booth had a focus on

Ada & Zangemann too. But the highlight this month was in Italy: our

Italian community celebrated three years with Ada at an event in Pesaro

with more than 50 primary school kids… and ice cream for everyone!

One last recommendation if you are a German speaker (also good for

practising your German skills 😉): [listen

to the latest episode of the Engineering Kiosk podcast, featuring Ada

& Zangemann!](https://engineeringkiosk.dev/podcast/episode/270-ada-und-zangemann-ein-m%C3%A4rchen-%C3%BCber-software-skateboards-und-himbeereis-mit-matthias-kirschner-von-der-fsfe/?pkn=shortlink) There Matthias talks with Andy and Wolfgang about a

lot if interesting background details of this illustrated story.

### Your support helps us move our work forward

We may be behind the wheel, but you’re the ones keeping us moving

forward. You can also [support us](https://fsfe.org/donate/donate.en.html), [contribute to our work](https://fsfe.org/contribute/contribute.en.html), and [join our community](https://fsfe.org/about/groups.en.html). Are you using social

media? If so, do not forget to follow us there! You can also follow the

FSFE news in your [RSS Reader](https://fsfe.org/news/news.en.rss).

[Discuss this](https://mastodon.social/deck/@fsfe/116719202770316716)

## Tags

### Share and support

*Some services may be Free Software unfriendly and harm your privacy. [Learn more](https://wiki.fsfe.org/Advocacy/ProprietaryWebServices).*

### Press

- [Press Room](https://fsfe.org/press/press.en.html)
- [Latest News](https://fsfe.org/news/news.en.html)
- [Free Software Basics](https://fsfe.org/freesoftware/freesoftware.en.html)

### About the FSFE

Free Software Foundation Europe is a charity that empowers users to

control technology.

Software is deeply involved in all aspects of our lives. It is important

that this technology empowers rather than restricts us. Free Software

gives everybody the rights to use, study, share, and improve software.

These rights help support other fundamental rights like freedom of

speech, freedom of press, and privacy.

# 數十年努力的勝利、Apple 調查發現、法律工作坊成果與第 50 集 podcast

## 數位主權需要自由軟體

過去幾週，我們第二次獲准在歐盟法院就 Apple 相關案件提出介入（！）；同時，歐盟執委會也把「Public Money? Public Code!（公共資金？公共程式碼！）」原則納入其「技術主權套案」。請持續關注！一個新的歐洲聯盟即將啟動，而我們也是其中一員。

這個月一開始就有好消息：歐盟執委會在新發布的「技術主權套案」中，納入了自由軟體基金會歐洲分會（Free Software Foundation Europe, FSFE）的「Public Money? Public Code!」原則；該套案也包含新的「開源策略」。如果真正落實，這可能象徵一場典範轉移，讓公帑資助的軟體能以自由軟體形式釋出。不過，現在還不是可以鬆懈的時候：[它的成功將取決於具約束力的規則、長期資金，以及有意義的公民社會參與](https://fsfe.org/news/2026/news-20260603-01.en.html)。

然而，並非所有公共行政機關都抱持相同想法。英格蘭國民保健署（NHS England）基於擔心公開程式碼儲存庫可能被 AI 系統掃描、用來找出漏洞，已預設將多數公開原始碼儲存庫改為私有。FSFE 對此立場很清楚：[NHS England 不應把公共程式碼藏在閉門之後](https://fsfe.org/news/2026/news-20260504-01.en.html)。下架公開內容不會讓程式碼變得沒有人看過，也不會移除既有副本，更不是有效的安全措施。相反地，這會移除安全的一項根本支柱：讓獨立專家、研究者與其他公共機關能夠檢視、重複使用、改進程式碼，並回報安全問題的能力。

我們呼籲自由軟體社群透過簽署[給 NHS England 的公開信](https://keepthingsopen.com/)，要求他們維持程式碼開放，來推動撤回這項決定。社群反應相當強烈，在我們發出呼籲後的幾個小時內，就新增超過 500 份連署。不久後，英國 Government Digital Service 發布新的指引，明確指出公共機關應預設維持程式碼公開。

透過自由軟體實現數位主權，也是我們最新一集 Software Freedom Podcast 的主題。在這集中，Bonnie 與 Johannes 與 X-Road 的 Petteri 對談，討論公共行政中的自由軟體專案目前面臨的挑戰。[歡迎收聽！](https://fsfe.org/news/podcast/2026/episode-51.en.html)

你可能已經知道，儘管歐洲需要數位主權，[Next Generation Internet Zero（NGI0）等歐洲專案的資金卻遭到刪減](https://fsfe.org/news/2024/news-20240719-01.en.html)。我們很高興能分享這方面的好消息：我們最近宣布了一個新的歐洲聯盟，目標是打造具韌性、在地生長的歐洲科技生態系，也就是 Restack 專案。

在 Horizon Europe 架構下，[FSFE 是這項階梯式資助計畫的合作夥伴，該計畫旨在延續 NGI Zero 方法的優勢](https://fsfe.org/news/2026/news-20260528-01.en.html)。我們的角色將是為可能超過 200 個自由軟體專案提供法律與授權支援，並協助它們成長為更廣泛歐洲數位公地的一部分。

### 在歐洲捍衛互通性

> 「在對方已有多位介入者充分代表產業利益的情況下，FSFE 的存在是為了確保公民社會同樣能被聽見，並讓法院能在掌握完整圖像的情況下作出判斷。」代表 FSFE 參與 T-359/25 Apple 訴歐盟執委會案的律師 Martin Husovec 博士表示。

對歐洲的軟體自由而言，這是一項具有里程碑意義的進展：自由軟體基金會歐洲分會已獲准在歐盟法院 T-359/25 Apple 訴歐盟執委會案中提出介入。這次介入的目標，是捍衛歐洲的互通性與軟體自由；這也是 FSFE 第二次就《數位市場法》（Digital Markets Act, DMA）與 Apple 相關訴訟，在歐盟法院提出介入。[前一個案件（T-1080/23）](https://fsfe.org/activities/apple-litigation/apple-litigation.en.html)涉及 Apple 對其 DMA 義務與被指定為守門人提出較廣泛的挑戰；而本案（T-359/25）則聚焦於 DMA 第 6(7) 條下的互通性，以及歐盟執委會具體規定 Apple 應如何實務履行這些義務的決定是否合法。

延續我們在《數位市場法》上的工作，我們參與了在杜塞道夫舉行的 [SCiDA Conference](https://scidaproject.com/2025/10/23/call-for-abstracts-scida-conference-on-shaping-competition-in-the-digital-age-towards-best-practices/)。這是一場聚焦數位市場競爭的重要學術活動。FSFE 受邀在全體會議中介紹我們在 Android 互通性上的工作，凸顯這項工作與當前政策及學術討論的關聯性。

這場會議聚集了歐洲各地競爭主管機關的高階代表，以及歐盟執委會 DMA 執法團隊成員。會議提供了絕佳機會，讓我們強化與關鍵利害關係人的連結，並進一步提高各界對 FSFE 在數位市場與使用者控制自身裝置自由相關政策工作的認識。

想更了解 DMA 嗎？我們受邀參與 [「DMA Vox Populi」podcast 關於 DMA 檢討的第 5 集](https://media.fsfe.org/w/j1CDP2zKnH1Px5fKKnvsvM%C3%A7)。在節目中，Dario 討論歐盟執委會哪些地方做對了、哪些地方仍有不足，以及歐洲在軟體自由與互通性方面接下來必須做什麼。

### Youth Hacking 4 Freedom 2026

2026 年度的 [Youth Hacking 4 Freedom](https://yh4f.org) 正進入高峰。程式開發期間將在本月底結束，參與者終於可以喘口氣，而評審團也將開始評估他們的專案。今年 10 月，我們將在布魯塞爾的頒獎典禮週末見到本屆 6 位得獎者。

第五屆 YH4F 共有來自 21 個國家的超過 80 位參與者！我們已經迫不及待想看看他們開發出了什麼成果。我們也已經在規劃下一屆，敬請期待！

### 從各個舞台：Ada、數位主權、PIWO 與更多活動

5 月非常忙碌！我們的波蘭在地小組參與了 P.I.W.O.（Poznań Free Software Event，波茲南自由軟體活動），志工們設攤推廣自由軟體。雖然活動名稱可能讓人想到免費的「piwo」（波蘭文的啤酒），但參與者得到的是免費披薩。

在柏林，我們的小組舉辦了 Linux 展示日，讓大家可以試用 Linux 筆電，並獲得關於 Linux 筆電各種疑問的解答。

此外，除了參與 SCIDA，我們也在布魯塞爾參加了一場關於 DMA 的座談。在 CPDP conference 期間，我們參與了題為[「It takes two to tango: Public and private enforcement of the Digital Markets Act」](https://www.cpdpconferences.org/panels/it-takes-two-to-tango-public-and-private-enforcement-of-the-digital-markets-act)的[座談](https://www.cpdpconferences.org/panels/it-takes-two-to-tango-public-and-private-enforcement-of-the-digital-markets-act)，介紹我們在 DMA 執法上的工作，包括我們在[歐盟法院對 Apple 提出的訴訟](https://fsfe.org/activities/apple-litigation/apple-litigation.en.html)。

數位主權也是雷根斯堡一系列講座中的主題。在觀看動畫電影《Ada & Zangemann》之後，我們參與了關於這個主題的討論。

**FSFE 即將滿 25 歲！我們想和你一起慶祝！** 7 月 18 日與 19 日，歡迎到克拉科夫參加充滿自由軟體的一個週末，現場將有演講、交流，當然還有蛋糕！想知道更多嗎？請寫信給我們：contact@fsfe.org

Ada 也出現在多場活動中：我們在 Tübingen Digital Freedom Days 舉辦了電影放映與兒童工作坊，並設置攤位。在烏特勒支的 NLUUG conference，我們的攤位同樣聚焦 Ada & Zangemann。不過本月亮點在義大利：我們的義大利社群在佩薩羅與 50 多位國小學童一起舉辦活動，慶祝 Ada 三週年，還有冰淇淋分享給每個人！

最後，如果你會德文，或想練習德文能力，這裡有一個推薦：[收聽 Engineering Kiosk podcast 最新一集，主題是 Ada & Zangemann！](https://engineeringkiosk.dev/podcast/episode/270-ada-und-zangemann-ein-m%C3%A4rchen-%C3%BCber-software-skateboards-und-himbeereis-mit-matthias-kirschner-von-der-fsfe/?pkn=shortlink) 在節目中，Matthias 與 Andy、Wolfgang 聊了許多關於這本繪本故事的有趣幕後細節。
